-- It's generally bad style to use CREATE OR REPLACE unnecessarily.
-- Test what happens if an extension does it anyway.
-- Replacing a shell type or operator is sort of like CREATE OR REPLACE;
-- check that too.

CREATE FUNCTION ext_cor_func() RETURNS text
  AS $$ SELECT 'ext_cor_func: original'::text $$ LANGUAGE sql

	RIGHTARG = int4,
	PROCEDURE = intset_union_elem

CREATE FUNCTION "public"."recursion_test"(integer, integer) RETURNS "text"
    LANGUAGE "plpgsql"
    AS $_$
DECLARE rslt text;
BEGIN
    IF $1 <= 0 THEN
        rslt = CAST($2 AS TEXT);
    ELSE
        rslt = CAST($1 AS TEXT) || ',' || recursion_test($1 - 1, $2);
    END IF;
    RETURN rslt;
END;$_$
;

begin
  open c1 (p2 := 77, p1 := 42/0);
end $$ language plpgsql
;
